title: js-stellar-sdk before 16.4.0 and 17.3.0 refuses contract specs with UDT names over 60 bytes (pre-v30 XDR bound, not a defect)

target.versions_affected: none: 16.3.0 - 16.3.1 and 17.2.0 - 17.2.1 follow the pre-v30 definitions they are built on

entries.expected: decode the interface: the v30 definitions bound a UDT name at 1024 bytes
entries.observed: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: contract.Spec.fromWasm refuses the testnet contract's spec at the 63-byte qualified name (string byte length 63 exceeds maximum 60).

entries.expected: decode the interface: the v30 definitions bound a UDT name at 1024 bytes
entries.observed: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: contract.Spec.fromWasm refuses the 61-byte struct name (string byte length 61 exceeds maximum 60).

entries.expected: decode the interface: the v30 definitions bound a UDT name at 1024 bytes
entries.observed: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1, 17.2.0 and 17.2.1: contract.Spec.fromWasm refuses the 1024-byte struct name (string byte length 1024 exceeds maximum 60).

evidence.pre_fix: Conformance runner (xcc conform run --entries 'contract-spec/*'), spec level: reject_valid with reason length_exceeds_max, declared as a known divergence referencing stellar-xdr PR #312.
evidence.post_fix: 16.4.0, 17.3.0 and later decode the same specs (spec level conforms).
evidence.expected_basis: stellar-xdr v30.0 (4f524bbac80c781c06e4fb5fc93a2d0d331d6705) raised SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT from 60 to 1024 bytes (https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/pull/312, merged 2026-09-09).

history.note: Created by xcc findings new from the spec-level known divergences that reference https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/pull/312 and their failure rows.
The refusal follows the pre-v30 XDR definitions these versions are built on; later versions on the v30 definitions decode the same specs.

resolution.reason: Not a defect in js-stellar-sdk. These versions decode contract specs with XDR definitions older than v30, where a UDT name is a string of at most 60 bytes (SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT 60); they refuse a longer name exactly as those definitions require. stellar-xdr v30 raised the bound to 1024 (https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/pull/312) so that soroban-sdk 30 can write fully qualified type names, and js-stellar-sdk adopted the v30 definitions in 16.4.0, 17.3.0, which decode the same specs. A reader on older definitions refusing names the newer definitions allow is protocol evolution, not a bug to report; the guidance for readers is to move to the v30 definitions.
resolution.manifest_action: none: the refusals stay declared as known divergences on contract-spec/qualified-udt-names, contract-spec/udt-name-61-bytes and contract-spec/udt-name-1024-bytes (status fixed, reference stellar-xdr PR #312), each naming this record
